results.strategy_description: The Ionic Value Master Fund Ltd. (the “Fund”) seeks to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns by investing (long and short) in companies trading at compelling valuations relative to their long-term intrinsic value. The investment strategy incorporates rigorous fundamental analysis to identify key sources of idiosyncratic, industry and macro risks, as well as investor controversy; assess investment risk-reward; and identify catalysts for shareholder value creation.  The Fund employs a relatively concentrated portfolio construction approach, seeking to capitalize on market volatility to build significant positions. The investment strategy pursues “value” investing broadly, seeking a balance of traditional value and growth at a reasonable price, and emphasizes companies operating in attractive industries with solid balance sheets and stable cash flow generation.  The Portfolio Manager leverages his 20+ years of extensive experience tackling complex event-driven situations and generating proprietary, out-of-consensus views through disciplined financial, strategic, operational and legal due diligence.  While idea generation is generally company-specific (bottom-up), the Fund also implements disciplined top-down portfolio construction and risk management principles.

Jain Global is a multi-strategy investment firm founded by Bobby Jain following his tenure as Co-Chief Investment Officer at Millennium Management. The firm launched in July 2024 with offices in the United States, Europe, and Asia and seven businesses - Fundamental Equities, Commodities, Equity Arbitrage, Rates & Macro, Credit, APAC and Systematic. Jain Global seeks to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns in all market environments for its investors.

Jain Global also specializes in strategies that help banks reduce regulatory capital requirements. These include Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) transactions, CVA hedging, and other balance sheet optimization tools. Banks are motivated to offload certain risks due to regulatory, accounting, or balance sheet constraints. These transactions allow banks to redeploy capital into other profit generating activities, while offering investors access to diversified and hard-to-access credit exposures.

Jain Global engages in a wide range of these transactions across regions, asset types, and counterparties to maximize diversification and identify compelling opportunities. Proactive hedging - designed to limit drawdowns and reduce exposure during market stress - is a key part of the approach.

•	We allocate capital in what we believe to be, a balanced manner to uncorrelated, market-neutral sub-strategies that invest across a variety of asset classes, regions, and time horizons.  
•	We aim to balance capital across sub-strategies focused on targeting relative value opportunities within fixed income, equity, credit, volatility, risk arbitrage / event driven and commodities markets. Each asset class is overseen by a dedicated Product Head.
•	Each sub-strategy within the Fund is run by specialised portfolio managers or investment teams who operate independently, with the aim of mitigating overlapping positions and limiting pairwise correlations.

results.strategy_description:
The Fund’s objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns through three principal investment strategies: (1) the convertible strategy, (2) the credit strategy, and (3) the SPAC strategy. In pursuit of this objective, the Investment Manager employs a flexible, multi-strategy investment approach which stresses inter-disciplinary cooperation and teamwork and aims to deliver market neutrality, capital preservation and steady, non-correlated, returns. 
• The Convertible Strategy is primarily focused on convertible bond arbitrage, with the goal of capturing mis-priced equity volatilities or creating cheaply-priced synthetic puts. In addition, the Convertible Strategy focuses on mis-priced credit opportunities where we obtain long/short credit exposure to convertible issuers. We also invest in catalyst and event driven opportunities within global mid-cap convertible bond issuers such as buybacks, tender offers, debt for equity swaps and other balance sheet restructurings.
• The Credit Strategy invests in both arbitrage and directional trades across the capital structure of corporate bond issuers. This strategy also pursues opportunistic/catalyst trades resulting from corporate events such as those listed above. We invest in the entire credit spectrum: distressed, high yield and investment grade.
•We invest in SPAC units, at or after the IPO, and trade or hold the shares and warrants that make up the units.  Investors in SPAC IPO shares can get their initial investment back if they don’t like the SPAC’s acquisition target, but have the option to participate in the equity upside if the SPAC shares trade higher; in that way, investments in SPACs have a return profile that is similar to that of convertible securities.

Linden utilizes a non-siloed, multi strategy approach to allocating risk capital among the three strategies. We seek to reposition the portfolio based on changing market conditions so that the weighting of each strategy varies depending on the perceived investment opportunities at any given time. The investment process is a collaborative effort between the portfolio managers, research and legal analysts and our trading team. Many of our investment ideas originate with a proprietary, quantitative model which screens the target global investment universe for securities that appear attractive. Linden then performs bottom up fundamental analysis so as to make a qualitative assessment of the risks/rewards of each opportunity. Linden seeks to adhere to a strict risk discipline. In an effort to limit downside exposure, Linden utilizes both position level and portfolio level hedges including selling short equity and debt, owning CDS protection, equity options, and other related macro hedges.

results.strategy_description:
Magnetar Special Situations Fund (the “Special Situations Fund” or the "Fund") seeks to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns through thesis-driven, catalyst-focused investments across the capital structure, with a primary focus on stressed and distressed credit and select engaged equity situations. The investment approach targets opportunities where market inefficiencies, capital structure complexity, or operational and financial dislocation create mispricing that can be addressed through rigorous fundamental analysis and active, hands-on engagement. The strategy is positioned to be opportunistic and value-oriented, emphasizing downside protection and a disciplined hedging framework designed to mitigate exogenous risks, isolate idiosyncratic sources of return, and drive attractive outcomes across market cycles.

The Special Situations Fund is led by Austin Camporin, who spent more than 15 years at Elliott Management prior to joining Magnetar. We believe the Fund is distinctive due to its ability to uncover and act on complex opportunities in areas of the market that are often overlooked – particularly among small- and mid-cap capital structures where inefficiencies are typically more pronounced. Our approach is built on disciplined sourcing and rigorous selection, driven by internal idea generation from a highly experienced team, supported by custom screens and best-in-class tools. 

We screen approximately 1,300 companies using Magnetar Labs' proprietary analytics and market networks, with fewer than 1% of ideas progressing to funded positions. Each investment targets specific catalysts – refinancings, restructurings, governance changes, or
operational improvements – with contingency paths and multiple avenues to value creation. Where appropriate, we engage proactively across financial, operational, strategic, and governance dimensions seeking to align stakeholders and drive outcomes. We maintain flexibility to invest across the capital structure, from senior secured debt to junior credit and equity.

We believe the current market environment – characterized by a large pipeline of upcoming maturities, elevated distress levels, and fragmented capital availability – creates a timely and scalable opportunity set. Magnetar’s flat organizational model, cross-functional team, and institutional infrastructure enable us to pursue high-conviction investments with creativity, precision, and speed, which we believe provides a competitive advantage.

The Special Situations Fund is structured as a master-feeder fund, composed of a Delaware limited partnership (onshore feeder fund) and a Cayman Islands exempted company (offshore feeder fund), each intended to invest into a Cayman Islands exempted company (master fund).

results.strategy_description:
Magnetar's Systematic Investing team seeks to efficiently extract the return streams associated with traditional hedge fund strategies, in which Magnetar has extensive practitioner experience. We implement this using proprietary data sets to support our quantitative research process and, importantly, hedge fund infrastructure covering execution, analytics, financing, and operations. 

Our investment process prioritizes sources of returns that are tangible, understandable, and intuitive, in contrast to data-mined strategies prone to overfitting.  

We launched the Magnetar Systematic Multi-Strategy Fund LLC (the "Onshore Fund") in August 2017 and the Magnetar Systematic Multi-Strategy Fund Ltd (the "Offshore Fund") in November 2018 as part of a master-feeder structure to provide investors with a diversified set of these strategies in one vehicle (the Onshore Fund, the Offshore Fund and the master fund are collectively referred to herein as the "Funds"). 

Our intent in portfolio construction for the Funds is to create a diversified portfolio that 1) has the potential to deliver returns in many types of market environments; 2) endeavors to protect capital; 3) is relatively liquid, and 4) is lowly correlated to both stock and bond markets. The Funds have historically realized a low sensitivity to broader equity markets and a negative correlation to hedge fund crowding factors. results.name: Mercator Convergence Fund
results.strategy_description:
The energy transition represents a multi-decade capital cycle across global power systems. While energy has always enabled societal change, we are witnessing an ongoing transformation in the nature of energy sources and technologies, at a time where the industry is also seeking to accommodate a sharp inflection in power demand. 

The Mercator Convergence Fund, a long/short global equities mandate, was established to capitalize on this multi decade structural investment opportunity. Positioned across the breadth of electricity capex and supply chain, the Fund deploys risk across ca. 40-60 positions. With an average trade duration of 24-36 months, the Fund targets structural shifts across the global energy system where value creation unfolds over extended investment horizons. By underwriting themes such as the growth in energy generation, grid modernization, and critical hardware solutions, Mercator seeks to capture persistent dispersion between structural winners and losers with a thesis focused on compounding returns.

A disciplined portfolio construction methodology which applies a risk-weighted capital allocation framework is a further defining characteristic of the strategy. The Fund’s exposure is actively managed to capture compelling upside asymmetry and to protect capital by tactically de risking and rotating exposures through windows of opportunity.

results.strategy_description:
The objective of the NISA Global Equity Alpha Extension Fund is to provide enhanced global equity exposure through a well diversified, active, long/short equity extension strategy. NISA’s proprietary approach seeks to deliver consistent alpha by systematically exploiting market inefficiencies that have persisted across market cycles. This relies on combining durable structural opportunities with a meticulously engineered process designed to layer incremental value at every stage, including portfolio construction, execution, and risk management.

The portfolio construction process begins with the identification of fundamental, attitudinal, structural, and/or technical characteristics (“signals”) of securities within the investment universe that are potentially informative to each security’s likelihood to outperform or underperform the benchmark. These signals may include both known risk premia and more sophisticated or idiosyncratic signals. Once collected, signals are selected, combined, and weighted to create forecasts for each security. The individual security forecasts are then translated into portfolio weights designed to meet the portfolio objectives and include considerations for market frictions and other trading dynamics. Diversification is prioritized within the portfolio construction process in order to protect against security specific events and other unknown risks.

This process seeks to construct a portfolio where the securities deemed most likely to outperform the benchmark are overweighted and the securities deemed most likely to underperform the benchmark are underweighted. NISA will often short the underweighted securities in order to implement the desired portfolio construction in relation to the benchmark, and as a result, introduce leverage into the portfolio. The gross and net amount of leverage utilized within the portfolio can vary over time and are adjusted in response to the market environment as a means to help control the portfolio's risk characteristics.

The strategy's investment objectives include a 3% tracking error target, 1.0 net of fee information ratio, and a beta of 1.0 to the MSCI World IMI Index (net) benchmark.

It invests in global macro themes, using a top-down approach, striving to construct macro-analytical frameworks that incorporate the rapidly changing macroeconomic conditions around the world and the significant idiosyncrasies of large global actors such as China. Trades are expressed via highly-liquid instruments such as FX, equity indices, equity baskets, commodities, fixed income, and rates. The strategy targets to generate net returns of 10-20% with volatility kept under 10%.

It is structured as a master fund and has two feeders, Arete Macro Feeder Fund and Arete Macro US Feeder Fund. We also manage the same strategy via a UCITS compliant vehicle (known as Tycho Arete Macro Fund), on a pari passu basis.

results.name: Ovata Equity Strategies Master Fund
results.strategy_description:
The Fund is an equity multi-strategy fund, focused predominantly on Asia Pacific markets. The Fund invests in public securities, mainly equities as well as equity derivatives and convertible bonds. The Fund utilizes an investment process that is based on a combination of the investment team’s significant experience as well as quantitative models.

Ovata Capital believes a combination of discretionary and quantitative investment processes, together with a mix of different time horizons and geographies, creates a robust and well-diversified investment business. Multiple investment specialists work collaboratively to provide optimal diversification of risk and return streams. The investment objective is to generate absolute return uncorrelated with general equity market performance. There are five equity strategies that aim to be complementary: Arbitrage, Relative Value, Event, Long/Short, and Capital Markets. Arbitrage profits from temporary mispricing anomalies across multiple securities on the same economic asset. Relative Value takes advantage of price misalignments in related but not economically identical securities, including cash and synthetic equities and convertible bonds. Event isolates securities that are undergoing a specific change of state along an acknowledged timeline. Long/Short identifies catalyst-driven short-term investment themes based on fundamental analysis, as well as quantitative and qualitative signals. The investment process seeks to isolate and capture alpha while minimizing exposure to systematic risks, such as market, country, sector, and style factors. Risk capital is dynamically allocated between the four strategies based on opportunities throughout the market cycle.
